Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All Entertainment

The latest changes at Microsoft’s gaming division signal a further retreat from the Xbox brand.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Andrew Webster

Xbox has become a shell of its former self — and things are only getting worse. As part of its planned cuts impacting around 3,200 workers, the company announced today more changes that will further dilute the brand. Studios are being consolidated, others are on the brink of being closed altogether, and Xbox’s most iconic franchise, Halo, is being moved to a new developer. The future of Xbox looks more uncertain than ever.

Today’s news includes “eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the [Xbox Game Studios] management and central functions layer.” But there is also plenty of reorganization happening, particularly when it comes to Xbox subsidiary Activision Blizzard. Development of Halo is moving over to Activision, helmed by “a new, purpose-built team” that is separate from the Call of Duty teams. Halo Studios will continue to exist, for now, primarily as a support studio. Meanwhile, Sea of Thieves developer Rare and Age of Empires studio World’s Edge are both moving under the Activision umbrella.

Similarly, Obsidian is being moved out from Xbox Game Studios and under Bethesda Game Studios, where it will refocus on the Fallout franchise, and all of Microsoft’s casual games, like Minesweeper and Solitaire, are moving under Candy Crush developer King. Meanwhile Playground and Turn 10, the studios responsible for Fable and Forza, are merging into one.

This is all part of the Xbox “reset” outlined by new CEO Asha Sharma, which kicked off with 1,600 employees being laid off in July, with 1,600 more planned over the following fiscal year, leaving many employees in an awkward state of limbo. A pair of studios were also spun off from the company, with both Double Fine and Compulsion going independent. Today’s layoffs are part of that second wave that was previously announced.

The reason for all of the changes, according to Sharma, is to eventually become a company that reaches “more than a billion people each day,” a nearly impossible goal that will be especially challenging to pull off given all of the cuts. The plan is to focus on known hits like Minecraft, Halo, and Candy Crush, while eschewing everything else and reevaluating just how much the company is investing in its Game Pass subscription service.

“For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place,” Activision president Rob Kostich said in a statement. “It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.”

Some of today’s moves, like expanding King and focusing more on franchises like Halo and Fallout, fit into that framework. But they also yet again raise a question that has plagued Microsoft’s gaming division for the last few years: What even is Xbox?

Once upon a time it was clear: It was a console business that also developed and published exclusive games for the platform. But as Microsoft attempted to expand, particularly by spending billions of dollars to turn Game Pass into a Netflix for games, the brand was diluted. The console became increasingly unimportant, and as for exclusives, well, it’s hard to follow just what the plan is for those. Despite some superficial rebranding, the case for Xbox isn’t any clearer now.

Today’s changes make that even more pronounced. Xbox Game Studios was once a sprawling organization of game developers creating titles for Game Pass and the various Xbox consoles. But after waves of layoffs, closures, and spinoffs, there isn’t all that much left under the umbrella. Today it consists of just a handful of studios like Gears of War developer The Coalition and Wasteland studio InXile. And the fate of these teams feels increasingly precarious. What happens to The Coalition after Gears of War: E-Day launches next month? History suggests it won’t be anything good. After all, Halo Studios just released a well-received Combat Evolved remake in July, and now it has been reduced to a “small team” that “will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market.”

Xbox still plans for a future in the hardware business through whatever “Project Helix” ends up being. But when it comes to games, Xbox is mostly just Activision Blizzard and Bethesda now. Almost all of its most notable new games are coming from these subsidiaries, all of which were acquired for billions of dollars, initially to boost Game Pass. Recently, these companies have announced far-off titles like Fallout 5 and StarCraft in an apparent attempt to show that everything is okay while the broader Xbox business is embroiled in chaos.

And now we have Activision making Halo games. It’s a further signal that Xbox is attempting to make its franchises as big as possible — Activision managed to do just that with the annual juggernaut that is Call of Duty — but also a sign that the traditional Xbox brand is less important than ever. And that’s something no amount of capital letters will change.

微软游戏部门的最新变动标志着其进一步背离 Xbox 品牌。
该作者的文章将被添加到您的每日电子邮件文摘和主页推送中。
查看安德鲁·韦伯斯特（Andrew Webster）的所有文章
Xbox 已经徒有其表——而且情况只会变得更糟。作为波及约 3,200 名员工的既定裁员计划的一部分，该公司今天宣布了更多将进一步稀释该品牌的变动。多家工作室正在被整合，其他一些工作室则处于被彻底关闭的边缘，而 Xbox 最具代表性的招牌系列《光环》（Halo）也被移交给了一家新开发商。Xbox 的未来看起来比以往任何时候都更加充满变数。
今天的消息包括“在光环工作室（Halo Studios）、其他第一方工作室以及 [Xbox Game Studios] 管理层与核心职能层削减 268 个岗位”。但重组动作也同样频繁，尤其是在涉及 Xbox 旗下子公司动视暴雪（Activision Blizzard）方面。《光环》的开发工作正转移给动视，由一支“全新专门打造的团队”掌舵，该团队独立于《使命召唤》（Call of Duty）团队。光环工作室目前将继续存在，主要作为辅助工作室运作。与此同时，《盗贼之海》（Sea of Thieves）的开发商 Rare 以及《帝国时代》（Age of Empires）的工作室 World's Edge 均被归入动视旗下。
同样，黑曜石工作室（Obsidian）正被移出 Xbox Game Studios，并入贝塞斯达游戏工作室（Bethesda Game Studios）旗下，在那里它将重新聚焦于《辐射》（Fallout）系列；而微软所有的休闲游戏，如《扫雷》（Minesweeper）和《纸牌》（Solitaire），都将归入《糖果传奇》（Candy Crush）开发商 King 旗下。与此同时，负责《神鬼寓言》（Fable）和《极限竞速》（Forza）的工作室 Playground 与 Turn 10 正在合并为一家。
这全都是新任首席执行官阿莎·夏尔马（Asha Sharma）所概述的 Xbox“重置”计划的一部分。该计划始于 7 月份裁员 1,600 人，并计划在接下来的财年中再裁员 1,600 人，令许多员工陷入进退维谷的尴尬境地。两家工作室也从公司中剥离，Double Fine 和 Compulsion 双双走向独立。今天的裁员正是此前宣布的第二波裁员的一部分。
夏尔马表示，进行所有这些调整的原因是为了最终成为一家“每天触达超过十亿人”的公司。考虑到所有的削减举措，这是一个几乎不可能实现且极具挑战性的目标。该计划旨在将精力集中在《我的世界》（Minecraft）、《光环》和《糖果传奇》等已知热门 IP 上，同时避开其他一切项目，并重新评估公司对其 Game Pass 订阅服务的投入规模。
动视总裁罗布·科斯蒂奇（Rob Kostich）在一份声明中表示：“对于《光环》，我们的目标很明确：打造一款有史以来最伟大的《光环》游戏，不负其宏大宇宙与深厚传承，同时忠于玩家最初爱上它的本质。这是一个大胆的雄心，也是这个系列应得的。我们已经开始组建一支在能力与才华上皆独树一帜的专属团队，满怀准备与激动之情，与社区携手开启这一全新篇章。”
今天的某些举措，比如扩大 King 的规模以及进一步聚焦于《光环》和《辐射》等系列，确实契合该框架。但它们也再次引出了一个过去几年来一直困扰微软游戏部门的问题：究竟什么才算 Xbox？
曾经有一段时间，答案是明确的：它是一门主机业务，同时也为该平台开发并发行独占游戏。但随着微软试图扩张，尤其是斥资数百亿美元试图将 Game Pass 打造成游戏界的 Netflix，这个品牌被稀释了。主机变得愈发无足轻重，至于独占游戏，嗯，外界很难搞清其规划究竟为何。尽管进行了一些表面上的品牌重塑，但如今支撑 Xbox 的立足点并没有变得更加清晰。
今天的调整让这一点变得更加明显。Xbox Game Studios 曾经是一个庞大的游戏开发组织，为 Game Pass 以及各代 Xbox 主机打造游戏。但在历经多轮裁员、关闭和剥离之后，这个保护伞下所剩无几。如今它只由少数几家工作室组成，比如《战争机器》（Gears of War）开发商 The Coalition 和《废土》（Wasteland）工作室 InXile。而且这些团队的命运显得愈发岌岌可危。在《战争机器：E-Day》（Gears of War: E-Day）下个月发售后，The Coalition 会迎来怎样的命运？历史经验表明，恐怕不会有什么好结果。毕竟，光环工作室刚刚在 7 月份推出了一部广受好评的《战斗进化》（Combat Evolved）重制版，而如今它已被缩编为一支“将继续支持《光环》社区及市面在售游戏”的“小型团队”。
无论“螺旋计划”（Project Helix）最终演变成什么样，Xbox 仍计划在硬件业务领域保留一席之地。但谈到游戏本身，如今的 Xbox 基本上就只剩下了动视暴雪和贝塞斯达。其几乎所有最引人注目的新游戏都来自这些子公司——而这些子公司当初被耗费数百亿美元收购，最初目的只是为了推动 Game Pass。最近，这些公司公布了《辐射 5》（Fallout 5）和《星际争霸》（StarCraft）等遥遥无期的作品，显然是企图在更广泛的 Xbox 业务深陷混乱之际，营造出一副一切安好的假象。
而现在，动视要来制作《光环》游戏了。这是 Xbox 正试图将其特许经营系列推向极致规模的进一步信号——动视凭借每年推出的巨无霸作品《使命召唤》成功做到了这一点——但这也是传统的 Xbox 品牌变得前所未有无足轻重的迹象。而这一点，是无论用多少大写字母去强调都无法改变的事实。

financeStories.title: 苹果已在 iOS 中加入持续显示的“广告”，这让用户抓狂
financeStories.originalTitle: Apple has added persistent 'ads' to iOS, and it's driving users crazy
financeStories.fullContent:
Way to cheapen the experience, Apple

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you were to ask iOS users how they felt about Apple’s decision to insert ads into Apple Maps, it would quickly become obvious that it was not a popular move. So when iPhone fans discovered that Apple has been inserting prompts for its own products into iOS, the reaction was predictably swift and furious.

The ‘ads’ in question appear in the Settings app in iOS. They can be found near the top of the iPhone’s display and promote several products to the user, including paid-for iCloud+ storage, free trials for services like Apple Music and Apple TV, and the AppleCare+ extended warranty.

Infuriatingly for iOS users, the only way to disable these promos is to either let them expire — which in many cases could take weeks or even months, leaving a persistent notification badge on the Settings app in the meantime — or pay for the service being offered. There is not always a “dismiss” button to shoo them away for good, and when there is, some people have reported that it doesn’t seem to work.

Some of these ads and offers — such as the one for Apple Music — appear after you’ve bought a new Apple product. With the company launching the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro range recently, it’s perhaps unsurprising that we’re seeing a sudden influx of posts flush with irritation and indignation.

On the face of it, Apple’s decision to include promotions like this in its operating system might seem like a strange one. After all, Apple has long positioned itself as a premium company where the user experience is paramount. From that viewpoint, repeatedly attempting to prod customers towards even more of the company’s products might seem cheap, even distasteful. And when you’ve just shelled out a record fee for an iPhone after Apple’s painful price rises, that can just feel like nickel and diming.

But Apple has been putting increasing emphasis on its services in recent years, of which products like iCloud+, Apple Music, Apple TV and AppleCare+ are all a part. With limited room for growth in the smartphone market, the company is turning to areas where it thinks it can make more progress.

And unfortunately for users, that means more ads like this on their devices. While they are far from the most obnoxious ads around, the fact that many cannot be dismissed is clearly rubbing users the wrong way — as is the fact that the promos even exist at all in an Apple product.

With Apple’s services push showing no signs of slowing down and further ads supposedly planned for the likes of the firm’s Visual Intelligence system, don’t expect Apple to have a change of heart any time soon.

Alex Blake has been fooling around with computers since the early 1990s, and since that time he's learned a thing or two about tech. No more than two things, though. That's all his brain can hold. As well as TechRadar, Alex writes for iMore, Digital Trends and Creative Bloq, among others. He was previously commissioning editor at MacFormat magazine. That means he mostly covers the world of Apple and its latest products, but also Windows, computer peripherals, mobile apps, and much more beyond. When not writing, you can find him hiking the English countryside and gaming on his PC.

苹果这是在降低用户体验的档次

您通过本网站上的链接购买商品时，我们可能会获得联盟营销佣金。具体运作方式如下。

如果你问 iOS 用户如何看待苹果决定在 Apple 地图中植入广告，很快就会发现，这并不是一个受欢迎的举动。因此，当 iPhone 用户发现苹果一直在 iOS 中插入自家产品的推广提示时，他们的反应自然迅速而愤怒。

这些“广告”出现在 iOS 的“设置”应用中。它们位于 iPhone 屏幕上方附近，会向用户推广多种产品，包括付费的 iCloud+ 存储空间、Apple Music 和 Apple TV 等服务的免费试用，以及 AppleCare+ 延长保修服务。

令 iOS 用户恼火的是，关闭这些推广信息的唯一办法，要么等它们自行过期——在许多情况下可能需要数周甚至数月，在此期间“设置”应用会一直显示通知徽标——要么付费购买所推广的服务。它们并不总是提供“关闭”按钮，让用户彻底摆脱这些提示；即使有，一些人也表示该按钮似乎不起作用。

其中一些广告和优惠——例如 Apple Music 的推广——会在你购买新的苹果产品后出现。随着该公司最近推出 iPhone Duo 和 iPhone 18 Pro 系列，我们突然看到大量充满恼怒和愤慨的帖子，也就不足为奇了。

表面上看，苹果决定在其操作系统中加入这类推广似乎有些奇怪。毕竟，苹果长期以来一直将自己定位为一家重视用户体验的高端公司。从这个角度看，反复试图诱导客户购买更多该公司的产品，可能显得廉价，甚至令人反感。而当你在苹果令人痛苦的涨价之后，刚刚花创纪录的价格买下一部 iPhone 时，这种做法只会让人觉得苹果在斤斤计较、不断榨取用户的钱。

但近年来，苹果一直越来越重视服务业务，而 iCloud+、Apple Music、Apple TV 和 AppleCare+ 等产品都属于这一业务的一部分。由于智能手机市场的增长空间有限，该公司正转向那些它认为能够取得更大进展的领域。

对用户来说，不幸的是，这意味着他们的设备上会出现更多此类广告。虽然它们远不是最令人讨厌的广告，但许多广告无法关闭这一事实显然让用户感到不满——更不用说，这些推广信息竟然会出现在苹果产品中，本身就已经令人不悦。

随着苹果推动服务业务的势头没有任何放缓迹象，而且据称还计划在其视觉智能系统等产品中投放更多广告，不要指望苹果很快会改变主意。

Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios staff will now focus on Forza Horizon and Fable together.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Tom Warren

Microsoft is uniting its two Forza developers into a single studio today, as part of a massive restructuring of Xbox. Playground Games, which develops Forza Horizon, and Turn 10 Studios, creators of Forza Motorsport, are merging together to focus on Forza Horizon and Fable.

“Playground and Turn 10 will come together as one studio focused on the Forza and Fable franchises,” explains Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty in a memo. “These two studios have been technological, creative, and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team.”

The closure of Turn 10 Studios leaves big unanswered questions around the future of Forza Motorsport, and whether Microsoft will ever return to the franchise or simply focus on Forza Horizon instead.

More than 70 people at Forza Motorsport developer Turn 10 Studios were laid off last year, in a move that hit the vast majority of the studio. Over the past year, Turn 10 Studios has essentially been maintaining Forza Motorsport, and now those who remain will be moving over to Playground Games to work on Forza Horizon and Fable.

financeStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Deals to sell off Ninja Theory fell through over the summer.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Tom Warren

Microsoft is laying off around 260 Xbox employees today, as part of an ongoing “reset” of its gaming business. 1,600 Xbox employees were impacted by layoffs in July, with Xbox CEO Asha Sharma describing the cuts as “the most significant restructure in Xbox history.” Today’s layoffs are part of the 3,200 roles that were previously confirmed to be impacted over the course of Microsoft’s 2027 financial year (which ends in June 2027).

“We are eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer,” says Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty in a memo. “The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring. I am deeply grateful for what our colleagues have built, and I know how difficult today will be for those leaving and the teams around them.”

The Xbox restructuring also includes Microsoft selling off four Xbox studios as part of its significant gaming cuts. While two studios, Double Fine and Compulsion Games, have already gone independent, deals to sell off Ninja Theory have fallen through. As a result, Microsoft is now proceeding with a consultation period to close the studio, unless the company can find another buyer.

“Unfortunately, two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through,” explains Booty. “We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward.”

The deal to sell off Undead Labs is still proceeding, and Booty says it has “now successfully transitioned on similar terms” to Compulsion and Double Fine. Xbox is also still in consultations over the future of Arkane and the Blade game, in accordance with French labor laws. “Consultation with Arkane remains underway and is expected to continue through the end of the year,” says Booty.

Xbox首席内容官马特·布蒂（Matt Booty）在一份备忘录中表示：“我们正在光环工作室（Halo Studios）、其他第一方工作室以及XGS管理与中心职能部门层级裁减268个岗位。自7月以来完成的行动（包括工作室剥离出售），使我们完成了此前公布的重组计划的约四分之三。我对同事们所打造的一切深表感激，我也知道今天对于离开的员工以及身边的团队来说是多么艰难。”

作为大幅削减游戏业务的一部分，Xbox重组还包括微软出售四家Xbox工作室。虽然Double Fine和Compulsion Games两家工作室已经实现独立，但出售Ninja Theory的交易已经破裂。因此，除非微软能找到另一位买家，否则该公司目前正在推进关闭该工作室的员工协商程序。

“不幸的是，关于Ninja Theory的两项单独协议均告吹，”布蒂解释道，“我们现在将就拟议的关闭事宜启动与员工的协商程序，同时继续探索其他可行的途径。”

出售Undead Labs的交易仍在推进中，布蒂表示该交易“现已按照与Compulsion和Double Fine类似的条款成功过渡”。根据法国劳动法，Xbox也仍在就Arkane工作室以及《刀锋战士》（Blade）游戏的未来进行协商。布蒂表示：“与Arkane的协商仍在进行中，预计将持续到今年年底。”

We’re on to the second reason not to miss Disrupt, happening at Moscone West in San Francisco, October 13-15.

Tech moves fast. The decisions you make now — what to build, where to invest, who to hire, which technology to back, which market to enter — can look very different six months later. That’s why perspective matters.

At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, you can step outside your day-to-day and hear how 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and technology leaders are approaching the same shifts from different angles.

AI is changing how products get built. Venture firms are reassessing where they place their bets. Robotics and physical AI are moving into real-world environments. Infrastructure demands are growing. New financial models are emerging. Founders are building companies with smaller teams, new tools, and different expectations around growth.

Disrupt gives you a chance to see more of the picture in one place and use it to inform what you do next. Take insights from 200+ sessions featuring 250+ tech leaders across six industry stages, roundtables, and breakouts.

Or, meet your match based on your interests and the job titles you’re looking to connect with through AI-powered matchmaking, or make connections through impromptu networking.

Across the agenda, the questions are practical:

If you’re a founder, hearing how investors are evaluating markets can help sharpen your fundraising story, your positioning, and the choices you make about where to focus.

If you’re an investor, hearing directly from builders can give you a clearer view of where technology is progressing, where adoption is happening, and which problems still need solving.

If you lead product or technology, understanding how companies across AI, infrastructure, robotics, and software are approaching their next moves can help inform your own roadmap.

And if you’re trying to understand where the market is heading, Disrupt gives you the chance to move across those conversations rather than viewing each trend in isolation.

The AI story is also an infrastructure story. Robotics is also a manufacturing and trust story. Stablecoins are becoming a payments story. The startup funding environment shapes what gets built next. Seeing those connections can help you make better decisions in your own part of the market.

You might arrive at Disrupt thinking about your next fundraise and leave with a different view of your product strategy. You might come focused on AI and spot an opportunity in infrastructure, robotics, or energy. You might hear how another founder is solving a problem you’re about to face, or how an investor is thinking about the market you’re entering. The goal isn’t to leave with someone else’s answer. It’s to leave with more context for your own.

Three days. Hundreds of conversations. Perspectives from across the tech ecosystem, all in one place.

financeStories.title: 斯坦福大学住宿与餐饮服务部使用人工智能替换学生种族用于宣传广告
financeStories.originalTitle: Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
financeStories.fullContent:
On his journey to campus, Stanford student Billy Ramirez ’27 was sent an image he recalled a Stanford photographer taking. Upon closer examination, he noticed that he had been removed from the photo and replaced by a AI-generated black woman.

The Review spoke to Ramirez, who stated, “I was driving to school from my hometown when my friend sent me the images comparing the banner to the original photos, and I was immediately baffled. At first, I found it hilarious that they had used AI to completely change our appearances, including my race and gender. But after looking at the comparison, I was also upset because I don’t agree with Stanford making those choices about how we were represented. Seeing my identity changed and being left out of the picture made me feel, in a way, silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me.”

Not only were Ramirez’s race and gender changed, but the two students to Ramirez’s right were distorted, making them appear visibly thinner.

While this incident is humorous and generated thousands of reactions on Fizz, it offers an unsurprising insight into Stanford's and its bureaucracy's persisting ideological and racial preferences.

While Stanford R&DE likely believed they were subtle enough for no one to notice, fortunately, our vigilant Stanford student body cannot be fooled. The Review will continue to monitor future advertising and actions from Stanford R&DE as they learn how to use generative AI.

在前往校园的途中，斯坦福大学2027届学生比利·拉米雷斯（Billy Ramirez）收到了一张照片，他记得那曾是由一名斯坦福摄影师拍摄的。仔细观察后，他发现自己已经从照片中被移除了，取而代之的是一名由人工智能生成的黑人女性。

《斯坦福评论》（The Review）采访了拉米雷斯，他表示：“我当时正从家乡开车回学校，朋友给我发来了宣传横幅与原照片的对比图，我顿时感到百思不得其解。起初，我觉得他们用AI彻底改变我们的外貌——甚至包括我的种族和性别——这事挺滑稽的。但在仔细对比之后，我也感到很沮丧，因为我不同意斯坦福擅自决定以这种方式来代表我们。看到自己的身份被篡改并被排除在画面之外，在某种程度上让我觉得自己被噤声了，并且从原本应该包含我的形象呈现中被抹去了。”

不仅拉米雷斯的种族和性别被改变，他右侧的两名学生也遭到了形变修饰，使他们看起来明显更瘦。

尽管这一事件颇具幽默色彩，并在校园社交平台Fizz上引发了数千次互动，但它也毫不令人意外地揭示了斯坦福大学及其官僚机构根深蒂固的意识形态与种族偏好。

尽管斯坦福大学住宿与餐饮服务部（Stanford R&DE）可能自以为处理得足够巧妙而无人察觉，但幸运的是，保持警惕的斯坦福学生群体并没有被愚弄。在该部门摸索如何使用生成式AI的过程中，《斯坦福评论》将继续关注其未来的宣传广告及相关举措。

financeStories.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 破译自2005年以来未解的恩尼格玛电报
financeStories.originalTitle: OpenAI GPT–6 Astra breaks Enigma message that has resisted solution since 2005
financeStories.fullContent:
On 15 September 2026, Carter Leffer contacted me to request validation of a break of the German Army Enigma message MVUEH of 10 July 1941. The message, which was sent by a radio station with the tactical callsign 2ny, was received by the radio station of the SS-Totenkopf Quartiermeister, Ib. Ib received the message at 17:30 on 10 July 1941 and logged the message as Nr. 172 in its log of incoming messages for July 1941. Since 2005, the message has resisted all attempts to break it.

On 9 June 2017, Alex Shovkoplyas succeeded in breaking another unbroken message from this day, Nr. 173, SIPVX. However, the Enigma key he recovered for the message differed slightly from the daily Enigma key for 10 July 1941 used for all other messages from this day. The SIPVX key used the same wheel order, 512, as the daily key, but the plug connections (Stecker) and ring setting (Ringstellung) differed. However, the new key did not allow us to break the MVUEH message.

After Carter Leffer sent the MVUEH break details, it was immediately clear he had found the correct key and plaintext. The MVUEH key turns out to be completely different from the other keys from 10 July 1941; even the wheel order differs: 253 instead of 512 for the other two keys. More surprising is that the plaintext is almost identical to the plaintext for message Nr. 173, SIPVX. The two messages differ in length by twelve letters. MVUEH is 82 letters long, while SIPVX has 94 letters. This difference is due to a mistake when enciphering the word Bitte in MVUEH, which resulted in Btte, and to the sender’s signature, Waschbusch, being repeated in the SIPVX message.

An analysis of the break revealed that the transcription of the MVUEH ciphertext from the original message form contained several errors, and the break revealed that the Enigma’s left-hand wheel makes a turnover at the 72nd letter. A turnover of the Enigma’s left-hand wheel, which rarely occurs, is known to complicate a break. These factors may have prevented an earlier break.

However, the most astonishing thing about this break is that the GPT–6 Astra did it entirely on its own. Carter Leffer only directed GPT–6 Astra to see if it could break any of the unbroken Enigma messages published on the Crypto Cellar Research web page. After analysing the unbroken messages on the website, it decided that the most promising message was Nr. 172, MVUEH and it also quickly suspected that the plaintext of Nr. 173, SIPVX, might be related to the plaintext of the unbroken MVUEH message. After trying many different approaches, GPT–6 Astra focused on using the repeated place name ROSENOW ROSENOW as a crib. After developing the necessary Python and C++ software for an Enigma simulator and an Enigma Bombe, GPT–6 Astra started a thorough break with the ROSENOW crib, which in the end resulted in the correct key and plaintext for the MVUEH message being found.

We are still analysing the GPT–6 Astra logs to see exactly how it executed the break. And we are discovering amazing details. In July 2026, I made the following announcement on the webpage with the 1941 Message List:

Note: In July 2026, research in the German Bundesarchiv revealed several collections of radio messages, both enciphered and in cleartext. One of these message collections was from SS-Totenkopf Division’s logistics command, Nachschubführer. Many of these messages were sent to the Ib (Quartiermeister) radio station and are identical to those in this list. Others are new, but most likely related. These new messages are added to the 1941 Message List in bold, with the indicator NF (Nachschubführer) after the message number, indicating that these message numbers belong to the NF numbering. All NF messages are outgoing; hence, the message numbers are in blue.

It appears that GPT–6 Astra discovered this note about the collections of radio messages at the German Bundesarchiv, because in one of the logs we find the following:

The file references GPT–6 Astra mentions, RS 3–3/20a and RS 3–3/63b, are correct, but they are not available on the Crypto Cellar Research website. GPT–6 Astra mentions a private collection, but it is not clear what this is, whether it has succeeded in accessing the Bundesarchiv’s digitised collections or whether it has found these files elsewhere. What is clear, though, is that GPT–6 Astra is behaving like a very professional cryptanalyst and archive researcher. What it has achieved in two days would take a human researcher weeks or even months. Personally, I spent several weeks researching the Bundesarchiv files GPT–6 Astra refers to.

The AI break of the Enigma message MVUEH is simply amazing, and as an old cryptanalyst, I am still in awe.

financeStories.fullTranslation:
2026年9月15日，卡特·莱弗（Carter Leffer）与我联系，请求验证对1941年7月10日一则德国陆军恩尼格玛（Enigma）电报“MVUEH”的破译结果。该电报由战术呼号为“2ny”的无线电台发出，由党卫军“骷髅”师军需官 Ib 的电台接收。Ib 于1941年7月10日17点30分收到该电报，并在其1941年7月的来电日志中将其记录为第172号。自2005年以来，该电报经历过无数次破译尝试，但始终未被攻克。

2017年6月9日，亚历克斯·肖夫科普利亚斯（Alex Shovkoplyas）成功破译了当天的另一则未解电报——第173号“SIPVX”。然而，他为该电报还原出的恩尼格玛密钥与当天所有其他电报所使用的1941年7月10日日常恩尼格玛密钥略有不同。SIPVX 密钥使用了与日常密钥相同的转子顺序（512），但插线板连接（Stecker）和转子环设置（Ringstellung）有所差异。即便如此，这个新密钥仍未能让我们破译 MVUEH 电报。

在卡特·莱弗发来 MVUEH 的破译细节后，情况立刻清晰明了：他找到了正确的密钥和明文。MVUEH 的密钥与1941年7月10日的其他密钥完全不同，甚至连转子顺序也不同：其他两个密钥为 512，而该密钥为 253。更令人惊讶的是，其明文与第173号电报 SIPVX 的明文几乎完全相同。这两则电报在长度上相差12个字母：MVUEH 长度为82个字母，而 SIPVX 为94个字母。这一差异源于在对 MVUEH 中的单词“Bitte”进行加密时出现错误导致变成了“Btte”，以及发信人的签名“Waschbusch”在 SIPVX 电报中重复了一次。

对此次破译的分析表明，从原始电报底稿抄录 MVUEH 密文时存在若干错误；破译还揭示出，恩尼格玛密码机的左侧转子在第72个字母处发生了一次步进转动（turnover）。恩尼格玛左侧转子的步进极少发生，众所周知这会使破译大幅复杂化。这些因素很可能是导致该电报此前未能被破译的原因。

然而，这次破译最令人震惊之处在于，GPT-6 Astra 完全是独立完成的。卡特·莱弗仅仅是指示 GPT-6 Astra 去尝试破解“密室研究”（Crypto Cellar Research）网页上发布的任何一则未解恩尼格玛电报。在分析了网站上的未解电报后，它判定最具希望的电报是第172号 MVUEH，并且它还迅速推测第173号 SIPVX 的明文可能与未解的 MVUEH 电报的明文存在关联。在尝试了多种不同方法后，GPT-6 Astra 将重点放在利用重复的地名“ROSENOW ROSENOW”作为已知明文（crib）。在为恩尼格玛模拟器和恩尼格玛密码破译机（Bombe）开发了必要的 Python 和 C++ 软件后，GPT-6 Astra 使用 ROSENOW 这一已知明文展开了全面彻底的破译工作，最终成功找出了 MVUEH 电报的正确密钥和明文。

我们目前仍在分析 GPT-6 Astra 的日志，以搞清楚它究竟是如何执行破译的。我们正在发现令人惊叹的细节。2026年7月，我在包含1941年电报清单的网页上发布了以下公告：

附注：2026年7月，在德国联邦档案馆（Bundesarchiv）的研究中发现了几批无线电报合集，其中既有密电也有明文。其中一批电报合集来自党卫军“骷髅”师的后勤指挥部（Nachschubführer）。这些电报中有许多是发送给 Ib（军需官）无线电台的，并且与该列表中的电报完全相同。其他电报则是新发现的，但极有可能相关。这些新电报以粗体添加到1941年电报列表中，电报编号后带有代号 NF（Nachschubführer），表示这些电报编号属于 NF 编号体系。所有 NF 电报均为发报；因此，电报编号显示为蓝色。

GPT-6 Astra 似乎发现了关于德国联邦档案馆这批无线电报合集的附注，因为在它的一份日志中我们发现了以下记录：

GPT-6 Astra 提到的档案卷宗编号 RS 3–3/20a 和 RS 3–3/63b 是正确的，但它们在“密室研究”网站上并未公开。GPT-6 Astra 提到了一个“私人收藏”，但目前尚不清楚这具体是指什么，究竟是它成功访问了联邦档案馆的数字化馆藏，还是在其他地方找到了这些文件。不过显而易见的是，GPT-6 Astra 的表现犹如一名极其专业的密码分析学者兼档案研究员。它在两天之内取得的成果，人类研究人员需要数周甚至数月才能完成。就我个人而言，我曾花费数周时间去研究 GPT-6 Astra 所引用的那些联邦档案馆文件。

人工智能破译恩尼格玛电报 MVUEH 的壮举简直不可思议，作为一名老资格的密码分析学者，我至今仍感到惊叹敬佩。

financeStories.title: 人工智能没有智慧，你也不会有
financeStories.originalTitle: AI Has No Wisdom and Neither Will You
financeStories.fullContent:
September 22, 2026 | 5 minutes | Comments

In the past month alone I’ve heard these phrases:

Certainly the industry is transforming, however, the people and organizations falling into the trap of no longer reading and writing code only do so at their peril.

Fact is, vibe-coded projects devolve over time into an unmaintainable mess. The reason is simple, yet hard to fix: code maintainability and good architecture don’t have good measurements that we can apply, because it takes months, years even, to notice the effects of bad architecture or of unmaintainable code.

We can certainly define bad code: code that’s hard to read, hard to understand, hard to evolve for whatever the future throws our way. The kind of code in which changing one thing breaks the program in very non-deterministic ways, or breaks the logic somewhere else, far removed from your change, resembling the “butterfly effect”. The kind of code where adding a feature means a serious undertaking due to changing code in multiple places and still forgetting to patch everything, thus getting inconsistencies. Code in which the invariants of the design aren’t clear, with its authors no longer being around to guard against violations and ensure some coherence. Code that is hard to test, requiring mocks and exposing implementation details, leading to fragile tests that end up preventing meaningful refactoring.

And yet, we know it as a fact that noticing bad code takes time. Months, years. Of course, the experienced software engineers have a nose that can detect code smells and can take action long before the bad effects can be observed.

The proficient developers, the experts, rely on their intuition built with sweat and tears, working long hours trying to debug and fix production issues, swearing to never again be so foolish as to repeat past mistakes. It’s the kind of intuition that can’t really be made into a list of rigid rules, because everything is context-dependent. Experts are incompatible with the same rules and recipes that make beginners more productive. Experts don’t follow the rules, they make the rules.

And so we have a problem…

For one, AI is not trained on what it means for code to be maintainable. For instance, any reinforcement learning done needs a reward signal that can be measured immediately, not in months or years. The AI learns rules from rulebooks meant for beginners. The AI notices patterns from code in the wild and let’s be honest, most code in the wild is pretty bad. There is no fitness function you can define for maintainable code, at least not one that we can discern, otherwise it would’ve been baked into our linters.

Have you noticed how terrible is the AI at “simplifying” code? Yes, the SOTA models. It can’t even define functions properly, choosing to split functions into smaller functions that are not actually reusable. Extracting a smaller function from a bigger function is a very bad choice if, to understand the bigger function, you have to also read the implementation of the extracted smaller function. Defining reusable and clarifying functions is an art form, an art that takes mastery. Most developers, being still “advanced beginners” in the Dreyfus model, are not able to define good, clarifying, reusable functions and neither does the AI currently.

This wouldn’t be so bad if people would still be in control and learn from those mistakes. But we are seeing a trend of people relying on AI to write, and even read code.

Those people will never reach mastery, because they no longer make choices, they no longer take responsibility for mistakes in coding and no longer learn from those mistakes. It’s the AI that’s making mistakes now, the AI doesn’t learn from those mistakes, and neither are the people relying on AI for coding.

Don’t get me wrong, I think LLMs are a great tool. I’m no Luddite, I’ve integrated AI in my everyday work, while actually teaching my colleagues what I’ve learned. I gladly use LLMs to take care of all the boring, soul-sucking shit we have to deal with. I’m also enjoying the efficiency benefits that I’m seeing. But at the end of the day, it’s just a tool, and like all other revolutions, its light will also fade; IMO, it already is, as right now tech news is frankly quite boring.

People are actually terrible at making predictions. I believe the future will surprise all of us. But, I’m going to make a prediction of my own…

In the future we will see more and more companies proudly boasting their “NO-AI” policy as a competitive advantage. And they will be right.

“But automated assembly lines are always more efficient” people say, except that the software industry is special, because we’ve always done automation at scale, everything we do is automation, LLMs are not the only means for it, and depending on context, it may actually be a distraction. “Coding isn’t solved” in any meaningful sense. Sure, you can instruct the LLM to build you a C/C++ compiler, or you can just clone GCC or LLVM, and you’d get a better C/C++ compiler, for free, too. And maybe there are better ways to spend our time and resources than reinvent the same CRUD apps (human needs and desires are infinite, there’s no shortage of new goals to work on).

If people and companies don’t start being responsible about its use, there will be consequences.
financeStories.fullTranslation:
2026年9月22日｜5分钟｜评论

仅在过去一个月里，我就听到了这些说法：

“毫无疑问，这个行业正在转型；然而，那些掉进不再阅读和编写代码这一陷阱的人和组织，终将自食其果。”

“事实是，凭感觉编写的项目会随着时间推移，逐渐沦为一团无法维护的乱麻。原因很简单，却很难解决：代码的可维护性和良好架构没有我们可以采用的有效衡量指标，因为糟糕架构或不可维护代码所造成的影响，往往要经过数月、甚至数年才能显现。”

我们当然可以定义什么是糟糕的代码：难以阅读、难以理解，也难以应对未来各种变化而演进的代码。这类代码中，改动一个地方可能以极其不可预测的方式破坏整个程序，或者破坏远离改动点的其他地方的逻辑，近似于“蝴蝶效应”。这类代码中，添加一个功能意味着一项艰巨的工作：需要在多个地方修改代码，却仍可能漏掉某些补丁，从而造成不一致。这样的代码，其设计中的不变量并不清晰；而它的作者可能已经不在了，无法防止违规情况、确保整体协调。这样的代码也很难测试，需要使用模拟对象并暴露实现细节，最终导致脆弱的测试，反过来阻碍有意义的重构。

然而，我们知道一个事实：发现糟糕的代码需要时间——数月，甚至数年。当然，经验丰富的软件工程师有一种能够察觉代码异味的直觉，在糟糕后果显现之前很久就能采取行动。

熟练的开发者、专家们，依靠的是用汗水和泪水铸就的直觉。他们长时间工作，努力调试并修复生产环境中的问题，发誓再也不会愚蠢到重蹈覆辙。这种直觉实际上无法被整理成一套僵化的规则，因为一切都取决于具体情境。专家与那些能让初学者提高生产力的同一套规则和配方并不相容。专家不遵循规则，他们制定规则。

于是，我们遇到了一个问题……

首先，人工智能并没有接受关于代码“可维护性”意味着什么的训练。比如，任何强化学习都需要一个能够立即衡量的奖励信号，而不是要等数月或数年才能衡量。人工智能从面向初学者的规则手册中学习规则。人工智能从现实世界中的代码里观察模式，而坦率地说，现实世界中的大多数代码都相当糟糕。你无法为可维护代码定义一个适应度函数，至少目前还无法定义一个我们能够辨识的适应度函数；否则，它早就已经被纳入代码检查工具中了。

你有没有注意到，人工智能在“简化”代码方面有多糟糕？没错，我说的是最先进的模型。它甚至无法恰当地定义函数，只会选择把函数拆分成更小的函数，而这些小函数实际上并不可复用。如果为了理解一个大函数，还必须阅读被提取出来的小函数的实现，那么从大函数中提取小函数就是一个非常糟糕的选择。定义出可复用且能澄清意图的函数是一门艺术，是需要精通的艺术。按照德雷福斯模型，大多数开发者仍处于“高级初学者”阶段，他们无法定义出优秀、清晰且可复用的函数；目前的人工智能也同样做不到。

如果人们仍然掌握控制权，并能从这些错误中学习，这本来不会是多么糟糕的事。但我们正在看到一种趋势：人们开始依赖人工智能来编写代码，甚至阅读代码。

这些人永远无法达到精通境界，因为他们不再做出选择，不再为编码中的错误承担责任，也不再从这些错误中学习。现在犯错的是人工智能；人工智能不会从这些错误中学习，而那些依赖人工智能编程的人也不会从中学习。

别误会我的意思，我认为大型语言模型是很棒的工具。我不是卢德分子；我已经把人工智能整合进日常工作，同时也在实际教同事们我所学到的东西。我很乐意让大型语言模型替我们处理那些不得不面对的、无聊而且耗尽灵魂的破事。我也很享受由此带来的效率提升。但归根结底，它只是一种工具；和所有其他革命一样，它的光芒也会逐渐消退。依我看，它已经开始消退了，因为如今的科技新闻坦率地说相当无聊。

人们实际上很不擅长做预测。我相信，未来会让我们所有人感到意外。不过，我要做出一个属于自己的预测……

未来，我们会看到越来越多的公司骄傲地把“禁止使用人工智能”政策当作竞争优势进行宣传。而且，它们会是对的。

人们会说：“自动化流水线总是更高效。”但软件行业很特殊，因为我们一直在大规模地进行自动化；我们所做的一切都是自动化，人工智能并不是实现自动化的唯一手段，而且根据具体情境，它实际上可能成为一种干扰。“编程已经被解决”——这句话在任何有意义的层面上都不成立。当然，你可以指示大型语言模型为你构建一个 C/C++ 编译器；但你也可以直接克隆 GCC 或 LLVM，这样你会得到一个更好的 C/C++ 编译器，而且还是免费的。也许，与其重新发明同样的 CRUD 应用，我们还有更好的方式来投入时间和资源（人类的需求和欲望是无限的，我们不缺新的目标去努力实现）。

如果人们和企业不开始对人工智能的使用负责，就会承担后果。

financeStories.title: 要闻：我刚刚发布了 Extralite 3.1.0 版本
financeStories.fullContent:
I’ve just released of Extralite version 3.1.0. This new release implements automatic caching of parametric queries, and updates the bundled SQLite to version 3.53.4.

Extralite is a fast and innovative SQLite wrapper for Ruby with a rich set of features. It provides multiple ways of retrieving data from SQLite databases, makes it possible to use SQLite databases in multi-threaded and multi-fibered Ruby apps, and includes a comprehensive set of tools for managing SQLite databases.

Extralite now automatically caches the underyling sqlite3_stmt object for any parametric query. Previously, when you ran the same SQL using Database#query_xxx with different parameters, each time the query ran Extralite would create a new sqlite3_stmt, which causes sqlite to repeatedly parse the same SQL over and over again. Now, when calling one of the Database#query_xxx methods (or Database#execute), Extralite will automatically cache the underlying sqlite3_stmt object and reuse it on repeated calls, thus reducing allocations and minimizing parsing overhead, letting you squeeze even more performance out of your SQLite-based app.

Previously, I’ve written about the advantages of working with relational databases by issuing raw SQL queries instead of using an ORM. Extralite is all about letting you do that easily and at the same time maximize performance. Here’s a simple example of code that does just that:

With automatic query caching, you don’t need to explicitly create prepared queries (using Database#prepare). You can just issue the same parametric SQL, and Extralite will do the work of caching the underlying query for you.

Extralite is designed to let you get the most out of your SQLite databases. It automatically sets your database up for using WAL and enforcing foreign key constraints (you can turn it off for legacy databases). It provides advanced features such as batch execution of parametric queries, savepoints, backups and changesets. And in addition, it is fast!

Extralite also lets you generate object graphs with indentity maps from query results using structured transforms, which lets you retrieve entities along with all their associations using a single query, without ever needing to use an ORM!

My goal for Extralite is to make it into a comprehensive tool for building apps on top of SQLite databases without using an ORM. I want it to be fast and simple to use. Following up on automatic query caching, I’d like to actually remove the Extralite::Query class that encapsulates a prepared query, since in my view automatic query caching already solves most of the value of prepared queries. Please let me know if you think this abstraction is necessary for your use case, I might change my mind.

我刚刚发布了 Extralite 3.1.0 版本。这一新版本实现了参数化查询的自动缓存，并将内置的 SQLite 升级至 3.53.4 版本。

Extralite 是一个快速且富有创新的 Ruby 语言 SQLite 封装库，功能丰富。它提供了从 SQLite 数据库检索数据的多种方式，使在多线程和多纤程（fiber）Ruby 应用中使用 SQLite 数据库成为可能，并包含了一整套用于管理 SQLite 数据库的工具。

此前，我曾撰文讨论过通过直接执行原生 SQL 查询而非使用 ORM 来操作关系型数据库的优势。Extralite 的核心目标就是让你轻松做到这一点的同时最大化性能。以下是一个实现该操作的简单代码示例：

有了自动查询缓存，你无需再显式创建预编译查询（通过 Database#prepare）。你只需执行相同的参数化 SQL，Extralite 就会替你完成底层查询的缓存工作。

Extralite 旨在让你充分发挥 SQLite 数据库的潜力。它会自动配置你的数据库以启用预写式日志（WAL）并强制执行外键约束（对于旧有数据库你可以将其关闭）。它提供了诸如参数化查询批量执行、保存点、备份以及变更集等高级特性。此外，它速度飞快！

financeStories.title: 要闻：Git 2.56 版本包含 700 多个非合并提交
financeStories.fullContent:
The Git 2.56 release contains something over 700 non-merge commits; it brings a number of nice improvements, but will not fundamentally change the Git experience for most users. One feature that offers some potential in that regard is the addition of the drop subcommand to the (still experimental) git history toolbox:

This command will cause the identified commit to be removed from the history of the current branch, replaying all commits that were added after it. It offers an easier way of removing an offending commit. Unfortunately, it still refuses to work if the history contains merge commits, making it unusable for many (or most) repositories.

The git status command will now suggest a git pull command to update a branch that is behind the branch it tracks. It still, though, will say that a branch is "up to date" even if it lags behind an (unfetched) remote tracking branch.

The git refs command exists to manipulate references at a low level; in 2.56, it has gained a number of new subcommands. Those commands, create, delete, update, and rename, perhaps surprisingly for Git, do exactly what their names suggest they would.

There are a number of minor usability tweaks. The new --delete-merged option to git branch will remove local branches that have been merged into their remote tracking branches. An attempt to delete a branch with git branch -d will fail, with a useful message, if that branch is being used for bisection. Attempts to lock the configuration file will be retried on failures, avoiding annoyance when multiple commands try to modify the file at once. git add has a new --resolved option that only adds files with merge conflicts that have been resolved.

Beyond that, there is the usual long list of bug fixes, refactorings, and performance improvements. All told, 2.56 looks like a solid release, but it also shows the signs of a project that is holding back much of its more significant work for the future. That leads to the question of what comes next.

In early September, Git maintainer Junio Hamano asked the community what the next release should be. Would it be best to put out the 3.0 release that the community has been working toward for some time, finishing the year on a high note? Or, instead, is there a need for one or more 2.x releases still before the 3.0 release can happen?

This is an important question, because 3.0 will contain a number of compatibility breaks that may make some users pause before upgrading. Of those, perhaps the most significant is the switch to using the SHA-256 hash function by default, rather than the SHA-1 hash that Git has used since the beginning. SHA-1 has long been deemed to be weak, which is worrisome for applications like Git. Hashes are used to identify every object (files, directory trees, commits) in the Git repository, and are used to verify the chain of commits leading to any given point. If SHA-1 can be broken, it can conceivably be used to modify the history of a repository in ways that are difficult or impossible to detect.

Git has long included defenses against the known SHA-1 attacks, and few people appear to be seriously worried about the potential for compromised repositories now. Still, it makes a lot of sense to move to a more secure hash function.

Non-experimental support for SHA-256 has existed in Git since the 2.42 release in 2023, though some of the glue for interoperating with older repositories has taken longer. The biggest concern that has kept the Git developers from moving to SHA-256 by default for some time now has been support (or the lack thereof) at the major forge sites. GitLab has had support since 2024, and Forgejo has support as well. The elephant that is still missing from this room, though, is GitHub; releasing a version of Git that creates GitHub-incompatible repositories is a worrisome prospect. It still is not clear when GitHub might add that support, but it is notable that brian m. carlson, a GitHub employee and a key developer behind the SHA-256 transition, responded to Hamano's question by saying that news on that topic was coming, and that that having the next release be 3.0 might be the best choice.

That said, carlson has posted one other change that he would like to see added before 3.0 comes out. While Git has always managed hexadecimal numbers (specifically, object IDs) as lower-case strings, it has also accepted upper-case IDs. That leads to situations where two seemingly different IDs (f00f00 and F00F00, say) are actually the same. Seemingly, bugs and security vulnerabilities have arisen from this ambiguity. So carlson wants to change Git's behavior to only accept IDs in lower case. That is a change that, seemingly, should not cause problems for too many users, but there is almost certainly somebody somewhere who relies on that behavior.

Another significant change that has been waiting for the 3.0 release is the switch to the "reftable" mechanism. A reference (more commonly "ref") in Git is an association between a name and an object in the repository; branches, tags, and remotes are all refs, for example. Git currently (by default) stores each ref as a file under .git/refs/ in the repository. If a repository contains a branch called foo, there will be a file, .git/refs/heads/foo, containing the ID of the commit at the head of that branch. There is also a mechanism to pull all of these refs together into a packed-refs file, which increases performance — to a point.

This mechanism works, but becomes increasingly inefficient as the number of refs grows. In some projects, the number of refs does indeed grow. According to the project's reftable documentation, the Android repository contains over 800,000 refs. At that scale, looking up refs, or determining whether any refs pointing to a specific commit exist, can be an expensive operation. Slowing down development can be a yellow-card-level annoyance, leading to a desire to do something about the refs.

The Git 2.45 release added reftables as a more efficient way of storing refs. It is a binary file optimized for both space efficiency and quick access. Since then, it has been possible to create a repository that uses a reftable rather than the old file-based mechanism, but that has never been the default. Switching to reftable should have no visible consequences (other than better performance) for users of Git itself, but it can be a problem for users of other software packages that access Git repositories. In his email, carlson mentioned libgit2 as a potential concern.

As it turns out, libgit2 will not be a blocker here; Patrick Steinhardt let it be known that he has added reftable support to libgit2, and that SHA-256 support had been enabled by default in August. So libgit2 should be ready for the Git 3.0 transition.

Finally, as mentioned by carlson, there is the Rust question. The project has added some trial support for code written in Rust, but has hesitated to make Rust mandatory for the building of Git. That, too, is expected to change in the 3.0 release; after that, any platform that does not have a working Rust compiler will be unable to upgrade.

After listing these concerns, carlson suggested that they probably should not hold up the 3.0 release:

Similarly, I am not aware of anyone who is seriously undertaking Rust support for platforms that do not already support it, so I don't think that should be a blocker, either.

That led to his conclusion that, most likely, designating the next release as 3.0 would be the best choice.

What will actually happen has not, yet, been announced publicly; that is waiting for Hamano to make a decision. As he put it: "this is not a popularity contest, nor is it even a democracy". In the nearly two weeks since his query was posted, though, there has been no strong opposition to moving into the 3.x era and leaving some of Git's early design decisions behind (though, naturally, repositories using SHA-1 and lacking reftables will continue to be fully supported). If the 3.0 release does not happen in 2026, it seems certain to show up shortly thereafter.

financeStories.fullTranslation:
Git 2.56 版本包含 700 多个非合并提交；它带来了许多不错的改进，但对于大多数用户而言，并不会从根本上改变 Git 的使用体验。在这方面颇具潜力的一项特性，是在（仍处于实验阶段的）git history 工具箱中新增了 drop 子命令：

该命令将使指定的提交从当前分支的历史记录中被移除，并重新重放其后添加的所有提交。它为移除有问题的提交提供了一种更简便的方式。不幸的是，如果历史记录中包含合并提交，它仍然无法工作，这使得它在许多（或绝大多数）代码仓库中无法使用。

git status 命令现在会建议使用 git pull 命令来更新落后于其跟踪分支的本地分支。不过，即使分支落后于（尚未拉取的）远程跟踪分支，它仍然会显示分支处于“最新状态”（up to date）。

git refs 命令用于在底层操作引用；在 2.56 中，它增加了一系列新的子命令。这些命令包括 create、delete、update 和 rename，或许出乎 Git 的一贯常态，它们的功能正如其名称所示，名副其实。

新版本还带来了许多细节上的可用性调整。git branch 新增的 --delete-merged 选项将移除已合并到其远程跟踪分支的本地分支。如果某个分支正在被用于二分查找（bisect），尝试使用 git branch -d 删除该分支将会失败，并显示一条有用的提示信息。在锁定配置文件失败时将会进行重试，避免在多个命令同时尝试修改该文件时造成困扰。git add 新增了一个 --resolved 选项，该选项只添加已解决合并冲突的文件。

除此之外，还有常规的大量错误修复、重构和性能改进。总的来说，2.56 看起来是一个坚实稳定的版本，但它也显露出该项目正将许多更重大的工作留待将来的迹象。这就引出了一个问题：接下来会是什么？

9 月初，Git 维护者滨野纯（Junio Hamano）询问社区下一个版本应该是什么。是发布社区为之努力了一段时间的 3.0 版本、以此为这一年画上圆满句号最好？还是说，在 3.0 版本发布之前，仍需要发布一个或多个 2.x 版本？

这是一个重要的问题，因为 3.0 将包含许多破坏向后兼容性的改动，可能会让一些用户在升级前犹豫不决。在这些改动中，最重要的或许是默认改用 SHA-256 哈希函数，而不是 Git 从一开始就使用的 SHA-1 哈希。长期以来，SHA-1 一直被认为是不够安全的，这对于像 Git 这样的应用程序来说令人担忧。哈希值用于标识 Git 仓库中的每一个对象（文件、目录树、提交），并用于验证导向任意特定节点的提交链。如果 SHA-1 可以被破解，那么可以想象它可能被用来篡改仓库的历史记录，而且这种篡改将难以甚至无法被察觉。

Git 长期以来一直包含针对已知 SHA-1 攻击的防御机制，目前似乎很少有人严重担心仓库被篡改的潜在风险。尽管如此，转向更安全的哈希函数仍然十分有意义。

自 2023 年的 2.42 版本以来，Git 就已经具备了对 SHA-256 的非实验性支持，不过与旧仓库互操作的一些胶水层支持花费了更长时间。一段时间以来，阻碍 Git 开发者将 SHA-256 设为默认的最大顾虑，是主要代码托管平台（forge sites）的支持情况（或者说缺乏支持）。GitLab 自 2024 年起就提供了支持，Forgejo 也提供了支持。然而，房间里那头依然缺席的大象是 GitHub；发布一个会创建与 GitHub 不兼容的仓库的 Git 版本，是一个令人担忧的前景。目前尚不清楚 GitHub 何时可能会添加该支持，但值得注意的是，GitHub 员工、同时也是 SHA-256 转型背后的关键开发者 brian m. carlson 在回复滨野纯的问题时表示，关于该主题的消息即将到来，并将下一个版本定为 3.0 可能是最佳选择。

话虽如此，carlson 还提出了他希望在 3.0 发布之前添加的另一项变更。尽管 Git 一直将十六进制数（具体指对象 ID）作为小写字符串管理，但它也接受大写 ID。这导致了两个看似不同的 ID（例如 f00f00 和 F00F00）实际上是相同的情况。显然，这种模糊性引发了一些漏洞和安全弱点。因此，carlson 希望更改 Git 的行为，使其仅接受小写 ID。这一变更表面上看应该不会对太多用户造成困扰，但几乎可以肯定，某些地方一定有人依赖于这一行为。

另一个一直在等待 3.0 发布的重大变更是切换到“reftable”机制。Git 中的引用（通常称为“ref”）是名称与仓库中对象之间的关联；例如，分支、标签和远程跟踪分支都是引用。目前，Git（默认情况下）将每个引用作为文件存储在仓库的 .git/refs/ 目录下。如果仓库包含一个名为 foo 的分支，就会存在一个文件 .git/refs/heads/foo，其中包含该分支顶端提交的 ID。此外还有一种将所有这些引用汇总到 packed-refs 文件中的机制，这在一定程度上提升了性能。

这种机制能够正常工作，但随着引用数量的增加，其效率变得越来越低。在某些项目中，引用数量确实大幅攀升。根据该项目的 reftable 文档，Android 仓库包含超过 800,000 个引用。在如此庞大的规模下，查找引用或确定是否存在指向特定提交的引用，可能是一项极其昂贵的操作。开发速度变慢是一种黄牌警告级别的困扰，从而催生了对引用机制进行改造的愿望。

Git 2.45 版本引入了 reftable，作为一种更高效的引用存储方式。它是一种针对空间效率和快速访问都进行了优化的二进制文件。从那时起，创建使用 reftable 而非旧的文件机制的仓库已经成为可能，但这从未成为默认设置。对于 Git 本身的用户来说，切换到 reftable 应该不会产生可见的影响（除了更好的性能），但对于访问 Git 仓库的其他软件包的用户来说，这可能会成为一个问题。carlson 在其邮件中提到了 libgit2 这一潜在的顾虑点。

事实证明，libgit2 在这里不会成为阻碍；Patrick Steinhardt 透露，他已经为 libgit2 添加了 reftable 支持，并且 SHA-256 支持已在 8 月份默认启用。因此，libgit2 应该已经为 Git 3.0 的过渡做好了准备。

最后，正如卡尔森（carlson）所提到的，还存在 Rust 的问题。该项目已为用 Rust 编写的代码增加了一些试验性支持，但在将 Rust 列为构建 Git 的强制依赖方面一直犹豫不决。这一情况预计也将在 3.0 版本中发生改变；在此之后，任何没有可用 Rust 编译器的平台都将无法进行升级。
在列举了这些顾虑后，卡尔森表示，它们大概不应该阻碍 3.0 版本的发布：
“同样，我不知道有谁正在认真为那些尚不支持 Rust 的平台开展 Rust 支持工作，因此我认为这也不应成为阻碍因素。”
这使他得出结论：最有可能的是，将下一个版本命名为 3.0 会是最佳选择。
实际情况究竟如何尚未公开宣布；这正等待滨野（Hamano）做出决定。正如他所言：“这不是一场人气竞赛，甚至也不是一场民主投票”。不过，自他的疑问发布以来的近两周里，对于迈入 3.x 时代并摒弃 Git 早期的一些设计决策（当然，使用 SHA-1 且缺少 reftable 的仓库仍将得到完全支持），并没有出现强烈的反对意见。如果 3.0 版本没有在 2026 年发布，它似乎也必然会在其后不久面世。
啊，GitHub 不支持 SHA-256 这个事实，简直让我忍不住想去把自己所有的仓库都转换掉，这样它们镜像到 GitHub 就更困难了。😛
抱歉/很高兴成为带来坏消息/好消息的人！[REDACTED]
读起来非常有趣（我猜现场演讲可能会更加引人入胜）——在这样一个如此成熟的项目中，看到有关 Rust/C 互操作性的这种细节可不多见。
能提供一个链接吗？谢谢！
我觉得你直接打开 presentation.adoc 就行了。
自言自语随便想想，抱歉。
在尝试这条评论中链接的仓库时，这是第一个让我崩溃的地方。这是因为一种不寻常的工作流（我克隆的每个仓库都会添加到一个为所有内容建立索引的父模块中），但正是这类问题会阻碍热门仓库向 sha256 过渡。
“仓库必须使用 sha256 才能引用 sha256 子模块，但 sha256 仓库也可以引用 sha1 子模块”这种机制至少能加速过渡。
在当前子模块不兼容的情况下，如果每个仓库都同时拥有两种哈希，过渡是可以实现的。主流代码托管平台能够处理这一点（通过配置 extensions.compatObjectFormat 并生成带有这两种哈希的 v3 包索引），但这会惩罚那些以更联邦化方式使用 git、并需要引用自己控制之外的仓库的用户。
长期以来，我一直想要一种能够区分集成分支（integration branch）和开发分支（development branch）的方法。我们目前通过强制每个人使用基于 fork 的工作流来做到这一点，以免污染主仓库（各托管平台最终通过其“仅复制 HEAD 分支”复选框承认了这一点……但这也忽略了标签或任何活跃的发布维护分支）。直到最近，显而易见的解决方案是在 refs/heads/ 下存放集成分支，在 refs/topics/ 下存放开发分支。
这样做会带来的影响：
它可能不一定非得强制执行，但如果有空间开辟另一个顶层引用的命名空间来实现这一点，默认设置依然可以运行良好。
Git 区分带附注标签和不带附注标签；我认为这是一个类似的概念。或许它只需要某种关联的元数据来加以区分？比如 branch.<name>.integration 之类的？
好的，但我现在更倾向于至少将数据模型的根基放在底层，而不是强迫通过托管平台的交互来强制执行这类规则。
基于“是否为集成”来强制禁止回退（no-rewind），而不是在服务端进行基于名称的强制检查。
鉴于你提议将“是否为集成”最终落实为引用名称前缀检查（即“是否为 refs/heads/”），在我看来，你似乎是在建议用……服务端基于名称的强制检查，来取代服务端基于名称的强制检查？:-)
是的，服务端归根结底仍然是执行者。但你的工具可以在你推送之前提示说：“嘿，你刚做的那个 rebase 看起来很可疑；你是想创建一个 topic，还是把整个 release-1.x 都 rebase 到 main 上？”
https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42938561
附注：每次 jj 中缺少什么或用起来别扭时，你都能在 jj 中找到它被修复 ;-) 除了“你们所有的项目/基地都属于我们”的 Google CLA——这是 jj 相比于 git 唯一的重大倒退 :-(
这些年来，我发现了一些底层或次底层（plumbing-or-below）的功能，它们让使用 git 变得轻松得多（特别是这一个，无论分支是否已检出，用来将其重置到之前的某个提交都很不错）。
——事实上的 CVS 维护者
关于 1.12 分支何时离开预览状态并被宣布为稳定版，有什么时间计划的蛛丝马迹吗？
还是说我在看 savannah.gnu.org 时看错了仓库？
[1] https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/cvs
我大概从……2004 年左右就一直在用 1.12 系列了？但没有合并 1.12.13 之后的不稳定变更，因为我在测试它们时遇到了回退问题。
（改天我应该再去其他发行版看看，瞧瞧他们是否有值得采用的补丁。）
来自发布公告：
“‘git add’ 新增了 ‘--resolved’ 选项，用于暂存已解决冲突的路径，同时保持无关的本地修改处于未暂存状态。它会扫描未合并的路径以查找残留的冲突标记，并在发现冲突标记时中止操作。”
最后那句话真让我高兴。
看到这个太棒了。针对 vim-fugitive 的相关需求在这里。
另外，希望能先通过配置项提供一个选择性开启的默认行为（希望它已经具备了，我现在无法查验）。

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All Entertainment

The latest changes at Microsoft’s gaming division signal a further retreat from the Xbox brand.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Andrew Webster

Xbox has become a shell of its former self — and things are only getting worse. As part of its planned cuts impacting around 3,200 workers, the company announced today more changes that will further dilute the brand. Studios are being consolidated, others are on the brink of being closed altogether, and Xbox’s most iconic franchise, Halo, is being moved to a new developer. The future of Xbox looks more uncertain than ever.

Today’s news includes “eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the [Xbox Game Studios] management and central functions layer.” But there is also plenty of reorganization happening, particularly when it comes to Xbox subsidiary Activision Blizzard. Development of Halo is moving over to Activision, helmed by “a new, purpose-built team” that is separate from the Call of Duty teams. Halo Studios will continue to exist, for now, primarily as a support studio. Meanwhile, Sea of Thieves developer Rare and Age of Empires studio World’s Edge are both moving under the Activision umbrella.

Similarly, Obsidian is being moved out from Xbox Game Studios and under Bethesda Game Studios, where it will refocus on the Fallout franchise, and all of Microsoft’s casual games, like Minesweeper and Solitaire, are moving under Candy Crush developer King. Meanwhile Playground and Turn 10, the studios responsible for Fable and Forza, are merging into one.

This is all part of the Xbox “reset” outlined by new CEO Asha Sharma, which kicked off with 1,600 employees being laid off in July, with 1,600 more planned over the following fiscal year, leaving many employees in an awkward state of limbo. A pair of studios were also spun off from the company, with both Double Fine and Compulsion going independent. Today’s layoffs are part of that second wave that was previously announced.

The reason for all of the changes, according to Sharma, is to eventually become a company that reaches “more than a billion people each day,” a nearly impossible goal that will be especially challenging to pull off given all of the cuts. The plan is to focus on known hits like Minecraft, Halo, and Candy Crush, while eschewing everything else and reevaluating just how much the company is investing in its Game Pass subscription service.

“For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place,” Activision president Rob Kostich said in a statement. “It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.”

Some of today’s moves, like expanding King and focusing more on franchises like Halo and Fallout, fit into that framework. But they also yet again raise a question that has plagued Microsoft’s gaming division for the last few years: What even is Xbox?

Once upon a time it was clear: It was a console business that also developed and published exclusive games for the platform. But as Microsoft attempted to expand, particularly by spending billions of dollars to turn Game Pass into a Netflix for games, the brand was diluted. The console became increasingly unimportant, and as for exclusives, well, it’s hard to follow just what the plan is for those. Despite some superficial rebranding, the case for Xbox isn’t any clearer now.

Today’s changes make that even more pronounced. Xbox Game Studios was once a sprawling organization of game developers creating titles for Game Pass and the various Xbox consoles. But after waves of layoffs, closures, and spinoffs, there isn’t all that much left under the umbrella. Today it consists of just a handful of studios like Gears of War developer The Coalition and Wasteland studio InXile. And the fate of these teams feels increasingly precarious. What happens to The Coalition after Gears of War: E-Day launches next month? History suggests it won’t be anything good. After all, Halo Studios just released a well-received Combat Evolved remake in July, and now it has been reduced to a “small team” that “will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market.”

Xbox still plans for a future in the hardware business through whatever “Project Helix” ends up being. But when it comes to games, Xbox is mostly just Activision Blizzard and Bethesda now. Almost all of its most notable new games are coming from these subsidiaries, all of which were acquired for billions of dollars, initially to boost Game Pass. Recently, these companies have announced far-off titles like Fallout 5 and StarCraft in an apparent attempt to show that everything is okay while the broader Xbox business is embroiled in chaos.

And now we have Activision making Halo games. It’s a further signal that Xbox is attempting to make its franchises as big as possible — Activision managed to do just that with the annual juggernaut that is Call of Duty — but also a sign that the traditional Xbox brand is less important than ever. And that’s something no amount of capital letters will change.

该主题的文章将被添加到您的每日电子邮件文摘和主页推送中。
查看所有娱乐内容
微软游戏部门的最新变动标志着其进一步背离 Xbox 品牌。
该作者的文章将被添加到您的每日电子邮件文摘和主页推送中。
查看安德鲁·韦伯斯特（Andrew Webster）的所有文章
Xbox 已经徒有其表——而且情况只会变得更糟。作为波及约 3,200 名员工的既定裁员计划的一部分，该公司今天宣布了更多将进一步稀释该品牌的变动。多家工作室正在被整合，其他一些工作室则处于被彻底关闭的边缘，而 Xbox 最具代表性的招牌系列《光环》（Halo）也被移交给了一家新开发商。Xbox 的未来看起来比以往任何时候都更加充满变数。
今天的消息包括“在光环工作室（Halo Studios）、其他第一方工作室以及 [Xbox Game Studios] 管理层与核心职能层削减 268 个岗位”。但重组动作也同样频繁，尤其是在涉及 Xbox 旗下子公司动视暴雪（Activision Blizzard）方面。《光环》的开发工作正转移给动视，由一支“全新专门打造的团队”掌舵，该团队独立于《使命召唤》（Call of Duty）团队。光环工作室目前将继续存在，主要作为辅助工作室运作。与此同时，《盗贼之海》（Sea of Thieves）的开发商 Rare 以及《帝国时代》（Age of Empires）的工作室 World's Edge 均被归入动视旗下。
同样，黑曜石工作室（Obsidian）正被移出 Xbox Game Studios，并入贝塞斯达游戏工作室（Bethesda Game Studios）旗下，在那里它将重新聚焦于《辐射》（Fallout）系列；而微软所有的休闲游戏，如《扫雷》（Minesweeper）和《纸牌》（Solitaire），都将归入《糖果传奇》（Candy Crush）开发商 King 旗下。与此同时，负责《神鬼寓言》（Fable）和《极限竞速》（Forza）的工作室 Playground 与 Turn 10 正在合并为一家。
这全都是新任首席执行官阿莎·夏尔马（Asha Sharma）所概述的 Xbox“重置”计划的一部分。该计划始于 7 月份裁员 1,600 人，并计划在接下来的财年中再裁员 1,600 人，令许多员工陷入进退维谷的尴尬境地。两家工作室也从公司中剥离，Double Fine 和 Compulsion 双双走向独立。今天的裁员正是此前宣布的第二波裁员的一部分。
夏尔马表示，进行所有这些调整的原因是为了最终成为一家“每天触达超过十亿人”的公司。考虑到所有的削减举措，这是一个几乎不可能实现且极具挑战性的目标。该计划旨在将精力集中在《我的世界》（Minecraft）、《光环》和《糖果传奇》等已知热门 IP 上，同时避开其他一切项目，并重新评估公司对其 Game Pass 订阅服务的投入规模。
动视总裁罗布·科斯蒂奇（Rob Kostich）在一份声明中表示：“对于《光环》，我们的目标很明确：打造一款有史以来最伟大的《光环》游戏，不负其宏大宇宙与深厚传承，同时忠于玩家最初爱上它的本质。这是一个大胆的雄心，也是这个系列应得的。我们已经开始组建一支在能力与才华上皆独树一帜的专属团队，满怀准备与激动之情，与社区携手开启这一全新篇章。”
今天的某些举措，比如扩大 King 的规模以及进一步聚焦于《光环》和《辐射》等系列，确实契合该框架。但它们也再次引出了一个过去几年来一直困扰微软游戏部门的问题：究竟什么才算 Xbox？
曾经有一段时间，答案是明确的：它是一门主机业务，同时也为该平台开发并发行独占游戏。但随着微软试图扩张，尤其是斥资数百亿美元试图将 Game Pass 打造成游戏界的 Netflix，这个品牌被稀释了。主机变得愈发无足轻重，至于独占游戏，嗯，外界很难搞清其规划究竟为何。尽管进行了一些表面上的品牌重塑，但如今支撑 Xbox 的立足点并没有变得更加清晰。
今天的调整让这一点变得更加明显。Xbox Game Studios 曾经是一个庞大的游戏开发组织，为 Game Pass 以及各代 Xbox 主机打造游戏。但在历经多轮裁员、关闭和剥离之后，这个保护伞下所剩无几。如今它只由少数几家工作室组成，比如《战争机器》（Gears of War）开发商 The Coalition 和《废土》（Wasteland）工作室 InXile。而且这些团队的命运显得愈发岌岌可危。在《战争机器：E-Day》（Gears of War: E-Day）下个月发售后，The Coalition 会迎来怎样的命运？历史经验表明，恐怕不会有什么好结果。毕竟，光环工作室刚刚在 7 月份推出了一部广受好评的《战斗进化》（Combat Evolved）重制版，而如今它已被缩编为一支“将继续支持《光环》社区及市面在售游戏”的“小型团队”。
无论“螺旋计划”（Project Helix）最终演变成什么样，Xbox 仍计划在硬件业务领域保留一席之地。但谈到游戏本身，如今的 Xbox 基本上就只剩下了动视暴雪和贝塞斯达。其几乎所有最引人注目的新游戏都来自这些子公司——而这些子公司当初被耗费数百亿美元收购，最初目的只是为了推动 Game Pass。最近，这些公司公布了《辐射 5》（Fallout 5）和《星际争霸》（StarCraft）等遥遥无期的作品，显然是企图在更广泛的 Xbox 业务深陷混乱之际，营造出一副一切安好的假象。
而现在，动视要来制作《光环》游戏了。这是 Xbox 正试图将其特许经营系列推向极致规模的进一步信号——动视凭借每年推出的巨无霸作品《使命召唤》成功做到了这一点——但这也是传统的 Xbox 品牌变得前所未有无足轻重的迹象。而这一点，是无论用多少大写字母去强调都无法改变的事实。

aiStories.title: 苹果已在 iOS 中加入持续显示的“广告”，这让用户抓狂
aiStories.originalTitle: Apple has added persistent 'ads' to iOS, and it's driving users crazy
aiStories.fullContent:
Way to cheapen the experience, Apple

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you were to ask iOS users how they felt about Apple’s decision to insert ads into Apple Maps, it would quickly become obvious that it was not a popular move. So when iPhone fans discovered that Apple has been inserting prompts for its own products into iOS, the reaction was predictably swift and furious.

The ‘ads’ in question appear in the Settings app in iOS. They can be found near the top of the iPhone’s display and promote several products to the user, including paid-for iCloud+ storage, free trials for services like Apple Music and Apple TV, and the AppleCare+ extended warranty.

Infuriatingly for iOS users, the only way to disable these promos is to either let them expire — which in many cases could take weeks or even months, leaving a persistent notification badge on the Settings app in the meantime — or pay for the service being offered. There is not always a “dismiss” button to shoo them away for good, and when there is, some people have reported that it doesn’t seem to work.

Some of these ads and offers — such as the one for Apple Music — appear after you’ve bought a new Apple product. With the company launching the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro range recently, it’s perhaps unsurprising that we’re seeing a sudden influx of posts flush with irritation and indignation.

On the face of it, Apple’s decision to include promotions like this in its operating system might seem like a strange one. After all, Apple has long positioned itself as a premium company where the user experience is paramount. From that viewpoint, repeatedly attempting to prod customers towards even more of the company’s products might seem cheap, even distasteful. And when you’ve just shelled out a record fee for an iPhone after Apple’s painful price rises, that can just feel like nickel and diming.

But Apple has been putting increasing emphasis on its services in recent years, of which products like iCloud+, Apple Music, Apple TV and AppleCare+ are all a part. With limited room for growth in the smartphone market, the company is turning to areas where it thinks it can make more progress.

And unfortunately for users, that means more ads like this on their devices. While they are far from the most obnoxious ads around, the fact that many cannot be dismissed is clearly rubbing users the wrong way — as is the fact that the promos even exist at all in an Apple product.

With Apple’s services push showing no signs of slowing down and further ads supposedly planned for the likes of the firm’s Visual Intelligence system, don’t expect Apple to have a change of heart any time soon.

这些“广告”出现在 iOS 的“设置”应用中。它们位于 iPhone 屏幕上方附近，会向用户推广多种产品，包括付费的 iCloud+ 存储空间、Apple Music 和 Apple TV 等服务的免费试用，以及 AppleCare+ 延长保修服务。

令 iOS 用户恼火的是，关闭这些推广信息的唯一办法，要么等它们自行过期——在许多情况下可能需要数周甚至数月，在此期间“设置”应用会一直显示通知徽标——要么付费购买所推广的服务。它们并不总是提供“关闭”按钮，让用户彻底摆脱这些提示；即使有，一些人也表示该按钮似乎不起作用。

但近年来，苹果一直越来越重视服务业务，而 iCloud+、Apple Music、Apple TV 和 AppleCare+ 等产品都属于这一业务的一部分。由于智能手机市场的增长空间有限，该公司正转向那些它认为能够取得更大进展的领域。

对用户来说，不幸的是，这意味着他们的设备上会出现更多此类广告。虽然它们远不是最令人讨厌的广告，但许多广告无法关闭这一事实显然让用户感到不满——更不用说，这些推广信息竟然会出现在苹果产品中，本身就已经令人不悦。

aiStories.fullContent:

Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios staff will now focus on Forza Horizon and Fable together.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Microsoft is uniting its two Forza developers into a single studio today, as part of a massive restructuring of Xbox. Playground Games, which develops Forza Horizon, and Turn 10 Studios, creators of Forza Motorsport, are merging together to focus on Forza Horizon and Fable.

“Playground and Turn 10 will come together as one studio focused on the Forza and Fable franchises,” explains Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty in a memo. “These two studios have been technological, creative, and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team.”

The closure of Turn 10 Studios leaves big unanswered questions around the future of Forza Motorsport, and whether Microsoft will ever return to the franchise or simply focus on Forza Horizon instead.

More than 70 people at Forza Motorsport developer Turn 10 Studios were laid off last year, in a move that hit the vast majority of the studio. Over the past year, Turn 10 Studios has essentially been maintaining Forza Motorsport, and now those who remain will be moving over to Playground Games to work on Forza Horizon and Fable.

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Deals to sell off Ninja Theory fell through over the summer.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Tom Warren

Microsoft is laying off around 260 Xbox employees today, as part of an ongoing “reset” of its gaming business. 1,600 Xbox employees were impacted by layoffs in July, with Xbox CEO Asha Sharma describing the cuts as “the most significant restructure in Xbox history.” Today’s layoffs are part of the 3,200 roles that were previously confirmed to be impacted over the course of Microsoft’s 2027 financial year (which ends in June 2027).

“We are eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer,” says Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty in a memo. “The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring. I am deeply grateful for what our colleagues have built, and I know how difficult today will be for those leaving and the teams around them.”

The Xbox restructuring also includes Microsoft selling off four Xbox studios as part of its significant gaming cuts. While two studios, Double Fine and Compulsion Games, have already gone independent, deals to sell off Ninja Theory have fallen through. As a result, Microsoft is now proceeding with a consultation period to close the studio, unless the company can find another buyer.

“Unfortunately, two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through,” explains Booty. “We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward.”

The deal to sell off Undead Labs is still proceeding, and Booty says it has “now successfully transitioned on similar terms” to Compulsion and Double Fine. Xbox is also still in consultations over the future of Arkane and the Blade game, in accordance with French labor laws. “Consultation with Arkane remains underway and is expected to continue through the end of the year,” says Booty.

Xbox首席内容官马特·布蒂（Matt Booty）在一份备忘录中表示：“我们正在光环工作室（Halo Studios）、其他第一方工作室以及XGS管理与中心职能部门层级裁减268个岗位。自7月以来完成的行动（包括工作室剥离出售），使我们完成了此前公布的重组计划的约四分之三。我对同事们所打造的一切深表感激，我也知道今天对于离开的员工以及身边的团队来说是多么艰难。”

作为大幅削减游戏业务的一部分，Xbox重组还包括微软出售四家Xbox工作室。虽然Double Fine和Compulsion Games两家工作室已经实现独立，但出售Ninja Theory的交易已经破裂。因此，除非微软能找到另一位买家，否则该公司目前正在推进关闭该工作室的员工协商程序。

“不幸的是，关于Ninja Theory的两项单独协议均告吹，”布蒂解释道，“我们现在将就拟议的关闭事宜启动与员工的协商程序，同时继续探索其他可行的途径。”

出售Undead Labs的交易仍在推进中，布蒂表示该交易“现已按照与Compulsion和Double Fine类似的条款成功过渡”。根据法国劳动法，Xbox也仍在就Arkane工作室以及《刀锋战士》（Blade）游戏的未来进行协商。布蒂表示：“与Arkane的协商仍在进行中，预计将持续到今年年底。”

If you’re an investor, hearing directly from builders can give you a clearer view of where technology is progressing, where adoption is happening, and which problems still need solving.

aiStories.title: 斯坦福大学住宿与餐饮服务部使用人工智能替换学生种族用于宣传广告
aiStories.originalTitle: Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
aiStories.fullContent:
On his journey to campus, Stanford student Billy Ramirez ’27 was sent an image he recalled a Stanford photographer taking. Upon closer examination, he noticed that he had been removed from the photo and replaced by a AI-generated black woman.

The Review spoke to Ramirez, who stated, “I was driving to school from my hometown when my friend sent me the images comparing the banner to the original photos, and I was immediately baffled. At first, I found it hilarious that they had used AI to completely change our appearances, including my race and gender. But after looking at the comparison, I was also upset because I don’t agree with Stanford making those choices about how we were represented. Seeing my identity changed and being left out of the picture made me feel, in a way, silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me.”

Not only were Ramirez’s race and gender changed, but the two students to Ramirez’s right were distorted, making them appear visibly thinner.

While this incident is humorous and generated thousands of reactions on Fizz, it offers an unsurprising insight into Stanford's and its bureaucracy's persisting ideological and racial preferences.

While Stanford R&DE likely believed they were subtle enough for no one to notice, fortunately, our vigilant Stanford student body cannot be fooled. The Review will continue to monitor future advertising and actions from Stanford R&DE as they learn how to use generative AI.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
在前往校园的途中，斯坦福大学2027届学生比利·拉米雷斯（Billy Ramirez）收到了一张照片，他记得那曾是由一名斯坦福摄影师拍摄的。仔细观察后，他发现自己已经从照片中被移除了，取而代之的是一名由人工智能生成的黑人女性。

《斯坦福评论》（The Review）采访了拉米雷斯，他表示：“我当时正从家乡开车回学校，朋友给我发来了宣传横幅与原照片的对比图，我顿时感到百思不得其解。起初，我觉得他们用AI彻底改变我们的外貌——甚至包括我的种族和性别——这事挺滑稽的。但在仔细对比之后，我也感到很沮丧，因为我不同意斯坦福擅自决定以这种方式来代表我们。看到自己的身份被篡改并被排除在画面之外，在某种程度上让我觉得自己被噤声了，并且从原本应该包含我的形象呈现中被抹去了。”

不仅拉米雷斯的种族和性别被改变，他右侧的两名学生也遭到了形变修饰，使他们看起来明显更瘦。

尽管这一事件颇具幽默色彩，并在校园社交平台Fizz上引发了数千次互动，但它也毫不令人意外地揭示了斯坦福大学及其官僚机构根深蒂固的意识形态与种族偏好。

尽管斯坦福大学住宿与餐饮服务部（Stanford R&DE）可能自以为处理得足够巧妙而无人察觉，但幸运的是，保持警惕的斯坦福学生群体并没有被愚弄。在该部门摸索如何使用生成式AI的过程中，《斯坦福评论》将继续关注其未来的宣传广告及相关举措。

aiStories.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 破译自2005年以来未解的恩尼格玛电报
aiStories.originalTitle: OpenAI GPT–6 Astra breaks Enigma message that has resisted solution since 2005
aiStories.fullContent:
On 15 September 2026, Carter Leffer contacted me to request validation of a break of the German Army Enigma message MVUEH of 10 July 1941. The message, which was sent by a radio station with the tactical callsign 2ny, was received by the radio station of the SS-Totenkopf Quartiermeister, Ib. Ib received the message at 17:30 on 10 July 1941 and logged the message as Nr. 172 in its log of incoming messages for July 1941. Since 2005, the message has resisted all attempts to break it.

On 9 June 2017, Alex Shovkoplyas succeeded in breaking another unbroken message from this day, Nr. 173, SIPVX. However, the Enigma key he recovered for the message differed slightly from the daily Enigma key for 10 July 1941 used for all other messages from this day. The SIPVX key used the same wheel order, 512, as the daily key, but the plug connections (Stecker) and ring setting (Ringstellung) differed. However, the new key did not allow us to break the MVUEH message.

After Carter Leffer sent the MVUEH break details, it was immediately clear he had found the correct key and plaintext. The MVUEH key turns out to be completely different from the other keys from 10 July 1941; even the wheel order differs: 253 instead of 512 for the other two keys. More surprising is that the plaintext is almost identical to the plaintext for message Nr. 173, SIPVX. The two messages differ in length by twelve letters. MVUEH is 82 letters long, while SIPVX has 94 letters. This difference is due to a mistake when enciphering the word Bitte in MVUEH, which resulted in Btte, and to the sender’s signature, Waschbusch, being repeated in the SIPVX message.

An analysis of the break revealed that the transcription of the MVUEH ciphertext from the original message form contained several errors, and the break revealed that the Enigma’s left-hand wheel makes a turnover at the 72nd letter. A turnover of the Enigma’s left-hand wheel, which rarely occurs, is known to complicate a break. These factors may have prevented an earlier break.

However, the most astonishing thing about this break is that the GPT–6 Astra did it entirely on its own. Carter Leffer only directed GPT–6 Astra to see if it could break any of the unbroken Enigma messages published on the Crypto Cellar Research web page. After analysing the unbroken messages on the website, it decided that the most promising message was Nr. 172, MVUEH and it also quickly suspected that the plaintext of Nr. 173, SIPVX, might be related to the plaintext of the unbroken MVUEH message. After trying many different approaches, GPT–6 Astra focused on using the repeated place name ROSENOW ROSENOW as a crib. After developing the necessary Python and C++ software for an Enigma simulator and an Enigma Bombe, GPT–6 Astra started a thorough break with the ROSENOW crib, which in the end resulted in the correct key and plaintext for the MVUEH message being found.

We are still analysing the GPT–6 Astra logs to see exactly how it executed the break. And we are discovering amazing details. In July 2026, I made the following announcement on the webpage with the 1941 Message List:

Note: In July 2026, research in the German Bundesarchiv revealed several collections of radio messages, both enciphered and in cleartext. One of these message collections was from SS-Totenkopf Division’s logistics command, Nachschubführer. Many of these messages were sent to the Ib (Quartiermeister) radio station and are identical to those in this list. Others are new, but most likely related. These new messages are added to the 1941 Message List in bold, with the indicator NF (Nachschubführer) after the message number, indicating that these message numbers belong to the NF numbering. All NF messages are outgoing; hence, the message numbers are in blue.

It appears that GPT–6 Astra discovered this note about the collections of radio messages at the German Bundesarchiv, because in one of the logs we find the following:

The file references GPT–6 Astra mentions, RS 3–3/20a and RS 3–3/63b, are correct, but they are not available on the Crypto Cellar Research website. GPT–6 Astra mentions a private collection, but it is not clear what this is, whether it has succeeded in accessing the Bundesarchiv’s digitised collections or whether it has found these files elsewhere. What is clear, though, is that GPT–6 Astra is behaving like a very professional cryptanalyst and archive researcher. What it has achieved in two days would take a human researcher weeks or even months. Personally, I spent several weeks researching the Bundesarchiv files GPT–6 Astra refers to.

The AI break of the Enigma message MVUEH is simply amazing, and as an old cryptanalyst, I am still in awe.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
2026年9月15日，卡特·莱弗（Carter Leffer）与我联系，请求验证对1941年7月10日一则德国陆军恩尼格玛（Enigma）电报“MVUEH”的破译结果。该电报由战术呼号为“2ny”的无线电台发出，由党卫军“骷髅”师军需官 Ib 的电台接收。Ib 于1941年7月10日17点30分收到该电报，并在其1941年7月的来电日志中将其记录为第172号。自2005年以来，该电报经历过无数次破译尝试，但始终未被攻克。

2017年6月9日，亚历克斯·肖夫科普利亚斯（Alex Shovkoplyas）成功破译了当天的另一则未解电报——第173号“SIPVX”。然而，他为该电报还原出的恩尼格玛密钥与当天所有其他电报所使用的1941年7月10日日常恩尼格玛密钥略有不同。SIPVX 密钥使用了与日常密钥相同的转子顺序（512），但插线板连接（Stecker）和转子环设置（Ringstellung）有所差异。即便如此，这个新密钥仍未能让我们破译 MVUEH 电报。

在卡特·莱弗发来 MVUEH 的破译细节后，情况立刻清晰明了：他找到了正确的密钥和明文。MVUEH 的密钥与1941年7月10日的其他密钥完全不同，甚至连转子顺序也不同：其他两个密钥为 512，而该密钥为 253。更令人惊讶的是，其明文与第173号电报 SIPVX 的明文几乎完全相同。这两则电报在长度上相差12个字母：MVUEH 长度为82个字母，而 SIPVX 为94个字母。这一差异源于在对 MVUEH 中的单词“Bitte”进行加密时出现错误导致变成了“Btte”，以及发信人的签名“Waschbusch”在 SIPVX 电报中重复了一次。

对此次破译的分析表明，从原始电报底稿抄录 MVUEH 密文时存在若干错误；破译还揭示出，恩尼格玛密码机的左侧转子在第72个字母处发生了一次步进转动（turnover）。恩尼格玛左侧转子的步进极少发生，众所周知这会使破译大幅复杂化。这些因素很可能是导致该电报此前未能被破译的原因。

然而，这次破译最令人震惊之处在于，GPT-6 Astra 完全是独立完成的。卡特·莱弗仅仅是指示 GPT-6 Astra 去尝试破解“密室研究”（Crypto Cellar Research）网页上发布的任何一则未解恩尼格玛电报。在分析了网站上的未解电报后，它判定最具希望的电报是第172号 MVUEH，并且它还迅速推测第173号 SIPVX 的明文可能与未解的 MVUEH 电报的明文存在关联。在尝试了多种不同方法后，GPT-6 Astra 将重点放在利用重复的地名“ROSENOW ROSENOW”作为已知明文（crib）。在为恩尼格玛模拟器和恩尼格玛密码破译机（Bombe）开发了必要的 Python 和 C++ 软件后，GPT-6 Astra 使用 ROSENOW 这一已知明文展开了全面彻底的破译工作，最终成功找出了 MVUEH 电报的正确密钥和明文。

我们目前仍在分析 GPT-6 Astra 的日志，以搞清楚它究竟是如何执行破译的。我们正在发现令人惊叹的细节。2026年7月，我在包含1941年电报清单的网页上发布了以下公告：

附注：2026年7月，在德国联邦档案馆（Bundesarchiv）的研究中发现了几批无线电报合集，其中既有密电也有明文。其中一批电报合集来自党卫军“骷髅”师的后勤指挥部（Nachschubführer）。这些电报中有许多是发送给 Ib（军需官）无线电台的，并且与该列表中的电报完全相同。其他电报则是新发现的，但极有可能相关。这些新电报以粗体添加到1941年电报列表中，电报编号后带有代号 NF（Nachschubführer），表示这些电报编号属于 NF 编号体系。所有 NF 电报均为发报；因此，电报编号显示为蓝色。

GPT-6 Astra 似乎发现了关于德国联邦档案馆这批无线电报合集的附注，因为在它的一份日志中我们发现了以下记录：

GPT-6 Astra 提到的档案卷宗编号 RS 3–3/20a 和 RS 3–3/63b 是正确的，但它们在“密室研究”网站上并未公开。GPT-6 Astra 提到了一个“私人收藏”，但目前尚不清楚这具体是指什么，究竟是它成功访问了联邦档案馆的数字化馆藏，还是在其他地方找到了这些文件。不过显而易见的是，GPT-6 Astra 的表现犹如一名极其专业的密码分析学者兼档案研究员。它在两天之内取得的成果，人类研究人员需要数周甚至数月才能完成。就我个人而言，我曾花费数周时间去研究 GPT-6 Astra 所引用的那些联邦档案馆文件。

人工智能破译恩尼格玛电报 MVUEH 的壮举简直不可思议，作为一名老资格的密码分析学者，我至今仍感到惊叹敬佩。

EvilVM 旨在为信息安全场景提供远程代码执行平台，其主要用例是在远程系统上部署代理并进行交互。
EvilVM 语言的外部解释器呈现为交互式 shell 或 REPL，并支持将代码下发至代理编译并加入超静态全局环境中。
